card.text: Pluto's largest moon, half its size, with a reddish north polar region.

introduction.text: Charon and Pluto always keep the same faces turned toward each other. James Christy spotted it in 1978, working with Robert Harrington.

normal.title: Monochrome mosaic
normal.summary: Lighting is corrected, but local shadows remain; the unseen south is left empty.

enhanced-color.title: MVIC false-color mosaic
enhanced-color.summary: Near-infrared, red and blue bands in false color, sharpened with finer detail.

elevation.title: Stereo and shading terrain model
elevation.summary: Stereo and shading heights relative to a 606 km sphere; detail varies.

albedo.title: New Horizons modeled Bond albedo
albedo.summary: Modeled share of sunlight Charon reflects, 0.02 to 0.53; the legend ends at 0.1 and 0.5 saturate.

water-ice.title: Water-ice absorption
water-ice.summary: Depth of water ice’s 2.0 µm absorption; grain size also changes it. Not ice abundance.

ammonia.title: Ammonia-related absorption
ammonia.summary: Infrared contrast linked to ammonia-bearing material, including Organa’s ejecta, averaged over about 12 km.
